rules.description: RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#682, live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03 23:05–23:57, still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22): runs FIRST, ahead of merge-validated AND sweep-stale-validating (whose relative order is a documented #637 invariant — this rule preserves it by prefixing, never interleaving). A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix). NOT failure — failure paths exist; NOT pending-with-active-runs — the localAction probes every run on the head (hasActiveDispatchedRun pattern widened to all events) and skips while anything is in flight. localAction rerun_cancelled_checks re-runs (gh run rerun) the latest attempt-1 cancelled run per required context and posts a once-per-head marker comment citing the evidence — ONLY when the rerun set covers every cancelled context (a partial set defers the marker so the uncovered contexts stay actionable; #695). BEHIND (silent-update refreshes the head) and DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it) are excluded, and agent:rework defers to the rework leg. limit 2: the observed death takes two PRs per wave (fa#1202+#1203 in one 36-second push wave).

Validated-but-stale: armed (ai_validating) + validation concluded but BASE MOVED (BEHIND only). BLOCKED must NOT unarm: since #483 BLOCKED is a real verdict, and on a freshly armed head BLOCKED simply means 'required checks pending' — unarming there races validate-armed in the SAME tick and deadlocks the PR forever (live: fa pr-762 armed at 08:25:37, unarmed 08:25:58 by the BLOCKED match, re-armed next tick, loop). silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating and merge-validated needs CLEAN, so without this unarm a genuinely moved base still deadlocks (live: fa pr-744) — BEHIND-only keeps that recovery and stops the self-inflicted one. gh-751 VERDICT-AWARE STRIP (live: fa #1295 — the arm was stripped FIVE times in one day with zero latches, [ai_validating]→[]→[ai_validating] yo-yo under a saturated CI queue): every main merge made the armed head BEHIND and this strip DISCARDED the head's ALREADY-CONCLUDED green verdict — it lost the race to the strip (merge-validated needs CLEAN; validated-green sits later and excludes pr_approved), silent-update refreshed, validate-fresh re-armed, the next merge re-struck: a full re-validation per main merge. The action now probes the head's dispatched validation runs before stripping: a GREEN run ANYWHERE on the head latches ai_validated instead of the bare unarm — not only the newest run: gh-748 showed two workflow_dispatch runs landing on ONE head seconds apart, and the latch consumer (validate-armed's skipIfValidatedHead → hasSuccessfulDispatchedRun) accepts any completed-green run on the head, so the strip consumes that same facet (complete_validation parity — sweep_stale_validation's success-branch shape; the latch excludes the PR from validate-fresh, and validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head so the merge window re-flows without new CI); only when NO green run exists on the head (red / absent / in-flight / cancelled-only) does the bare unarm stand (refresh + re-validate recovery).

RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#637 aftermath, live fa pr-1174 2026-10-03): this rule MUST run before sweep-stale-validating — the 15-min staleness sweep eats every arm before the merge can consume it whenever the tick cadence slips past 15 min (night kicker slippage), looping arm→sweep→arm on a green merge-ready head. GitHub PR: validation green + CLEAN -> squash-merge (merge_pr verifies the sticky pr_approved latch on the PR; an un-approved green head latches ai_validated instead — see merge_pr). FIFO drain (#687).

RULE ORDER (owner directive 2026-10-04 'red yields the slot', live fa 11:0x: #1194 held ai_validating through repeated reds while #1215..#1223 sat FIFO-queued 40+ min): this rule MUST run BEFORE validate-armed — the unarm below frees the limit-1 mutex and (with the openPrs ioCache drop in the action) the arm rule's later query in the SAME tick sees the freed slot and arms the NEXT oldest approved PR immediately. Previously fail-validation ran after validate-armed: the arm rule scanned the still-occupied mutex every tick and the slot stayed hostage until the failed PR's rework cycle re-armed it. #637 rule-order invariant preserved: rerun-cancelled-checks stays first (#682/gh-682), and merge-validated still runs before sweep-stale-validating. GitHub PR: validation CI red on the head -> unarm ai_validating, report (with the 🔴 red-head counter marker — the validate_pr arm side skips heads with >= redHeadCap recorded reds), requeue agent:rework on the linked issue. pr_approved is STICKY (owner rule 2026-09): the reworked head re-validates and merges without a re-review — no token burn on review legs. Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial.

Stale-arm sweeper (live: fa #999 — ai_validating held 7h with a CONCLUDED green CI and no verdict consumed; the ai_validating mutex stayed held forever. unarm-stale-validation covers BEHIND only). ai_validating + the head's dispatched validation run CONCLUDED (success or failure — CANCELLED is never a verdict) more than staleMinutes (15) ago, arm never consumed → unarm. Success side: unarm + re-latch ai_validated (complete_validation parity — the merge window re-flows; validate-armed latch-skips on the unchanged head). Failure side: the standard fail path (report + machine-only rework re-arm). Fresh conclusions (<15 min) never sweep: the check-visibility/verdict race window — the same-tick verdict rules (merge-validated / fail-validation / validated-green) own those. BEHIND excluded: unarm-stale-validation owns the moved-base recovery.

Every open non-draft PR behind main gets a silent branch refresh with the workflow token (pushes trigger no workflows, so freshness is free); validating PRs are excluded so the validation head never moves mid-run. mergeState is BEHIND only: the prStatus deterministic override computes BEHIND from base freshness (immune to the REST BEHIND/BLOCKED flip-flop this rule used to paper over with both values), and BLOCKED is now a REAL verdict (fresh head, required checks pending/red) — updating those would no-op-clone every pending PR on every tick. Limit 20 (owner 2026-09-22): silent pushes fire no CI — refreshing every BEHIND head every tick is free and keeps PRs merge-ready, so the merge window never waits for a refresh first. STICKY PARK (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923): before refreshing, a GUEST PR whose current head has RED checks is labeled validation_failed (idempotent, the head SHA noted in a one-time comment) — validate-armed excludes the label and no validation CI is dispatched for it at all; the label is REMOVED only when the LAST SUBSTANTIVE commit (machine-authored merges of main walked back past, dmtools-agents#681) is a NON-machine push NEWER than the park, so the SM's own silent-updates — bot merges or re-arms — never clear a red guest's park. Machine-authored PRs never get the label (fa pushes their heads).

Sticky-park RESET for NON-BEHIND heads (dmtools-agents, live fa 2026-10-03): the human-push unpark probe lives inside update_branch, but silent-update-behind only matches mergeState BEHIND — a guest PR whose fix commit lands on the SAME base (not behind) NEVER runs the RESET and the park outlives any human push (live: vendor pushed 16:01 to five parked approved PRs; 2h later not one label cleared, the whole approved FIFO frozen). This rule routes every parked non-validating PR through update_branch's RESET probe regardless of merge state: a NON-machine SUBSTANTIVE push NEWER than the newest park event clears the label — the probe walks back past machine-authored merges of main to the last substantive commit: a bot merge BURIES the retrigger, never replaces it (dmtools-agents#681, live fa#1213 2026-10-03 22:56–23:10: retrigger 7ecf11d7 buried by bot merge b3f9c6b5 before the next tick, the old head-keyed probe declined and the park survived 4 real ticks); then validate-armed picks the PR up on a later pass (this rule never dispatches CI itself); machine pushes and stale heads keep the park (fail closed). The silent branch refresh inside the action is a no-op for a non-BEHIND head (git merge reports up-to-date, no push).

Post-approval merge window — OWNER FIFO RULE (2026-09-22): lead the OLDEST approved PR all the way to merge; never validate other approved PRs meanwhile (the merge moves the base — they would re-validate anyway). Advance to the next approved ONLY when the oldest is DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it) or its validation went RED (rework leg fixes it) — both free this slot while the oldest repairs. BEHIND/DIRTY excluded here: silent-update refreshes BEHIND heads first; conflicted heads can never reach CLEAN. Mutex ai_validating = one validation at a time; the action re-verifies that mutex at ARM time on a LIVE list (owner directive 2026-10-04, live fa 12:0x: #1194 + #1215 both armed after a manual strip — the query-time scan read the stale cached list). RED YIELDS THE SLOT (owner directive 2026-10-04): a candidate whose CURRENT head SHA already went red redHeadCap (default 3) times — counted from the 🔴 markers on its fail reports — is SKIPPED until a NEW head lands; jobParams.redHeadSkip=false disables. validation_failed excluded (owner 2026-09-27, live: fa#923 — a GUEST PR whose head went red cycles arm→CI red→silent-update→re-arm forever, holding this limit-1 slot hostage; the silent-update action labels such guests validation_failed and they stay parked until a NON-MACHINE push moves the head).

Armed head moved mid-validation (double silent-update, rework push): the green run no longer covers the head, checks read 'none' on it, but the ai_validating arm persists — no rule matched and the PR stalled until a manual disarm (live: dart pr-194, 15:06 — tick processed 0). Re-dispatch the CI on the CURRENT head. pending ALSO matches now (dmtools-agents#632, live fa#1161 2026-10-02: a cancelled-only rollup folds pending and NO rule re-dispatched — the lost-run state is checks:none OR pending with nothing in flight; validate_pr's hasActiveDispatchedRun probe fail-opens the duplicate guard, so a genuinely in-flight run is never double-dispatched). BEHIND/DIRTY excluded like validate-armed. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs held ai_validating simultaneously: 922/923/930/932/934/948/961, +1 arm per tick): this rule previously ran with NO mutex because the global mutex scan sees the rule's own armed target and self-blocks 100% of the time — and its 'structural serialization' assumption (validate-armed's mutex guarantees <=1 armed approved PR) is FALSE once heads move: silent-update / BEHIND unarm races / guest pushes keep feeding checks=none states, and each tick this rule armed one more approved PR. The exclude-self mutex (githubSource) evaluates per candidate: it defers only while ANOTHER approved PR holds ai_validating. Exactly one armed approved PR = the candidate itself = the rule fires; a second approved arm anywhere = every candidate defers and the stack drains via merge-validated / fail-validation / unarm-stale.

Dead-zone fix (live: fa pr-922, 2026-09-26 — frozen in ai_validating for hours, ticks processed 0): the armed head's dispatched CI run was LOST (racing dispatch canceled by concurrency, or the gh workflow run CLI call failed silently — dispatchCiWorkflow cannot throw). Every existing check is green, but the required CI check is ABSENT from the head, so the rollup reads 'green' while REST mergeState stays BLOCKED. No rule matched: revalidate-armed wants checks=none, merge-validated wants CLEAN, fail-validation wants red, unarm-stale wants BEHIND. 'green' + not-CLEAN here means the arm is stale and the CI verdict is missing — re-dispatch (validate_pr's duplicate-dispatch guard skips if a run is already landing; the skipIfGreenCi flag stops the loop when a completed green CI run already covers the head and the blocker is some other workflow's required check). Armed+green+CLEAN must NOT match — that is merge-validated's merge — hence CLEAN is excluded. MUTEX with mutexExcludeSelf (multi-arm leak fix, live: fa 2026-09-26 — 7 approved PRs armed at once): same self-block reason as revalidate-armed made this rule ship mutex-less, and the same false singleton assumption let it feed the +1-arm-per-tick leak. The exclude-self mutex defers the candidate only while ANOTHER approved PR holds ai_validating; with the invariant restored this rule fires exactly on the one armed approved PR and never arms a second.

GitHub PR: head with no CONCLUDED validation (checks 'none' — fresh push, no CI — or 'pending' — the dispatch bridge's waiting check runs; pushes fire no CI) -> dispatch the CI workflow on the head + ai_validating marker. OWNER RULE (2026-09-23, validation economy): validate ONCE per PR — the first green is the ticket to review; after it the ai_validated latch excludes the PR here, silent-update keeps it fresh (no re-validation on refresh), and the single pre-merge validation lives in validate-armed (post-approve, current head). Red heads repeat this rule only after a NEW push clears the red. chore:pin PRs (factory lockstep bumps) are exempt: the factory suite gates them before the cut, and the next real PR validates the pinned content via silent-update.

GitHub PR: validation green but not yet approved -> latch ai_validated, unarm ai_validating. review-after-dev requires the latch + green checks, so review fires exactly once per validated head. Approved PRs are excluded (merge-validated / unarm-stale own them). Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): latch/unlatch verdicts in waves — pure label writes, nothing serial.

GitHub PR: branch conflicts with main (silent-update's git merge cannot land; mergeState DIRTY) -> the queue would stall forever — report and, for MACHINE-authored PRs, re-arm agent:rework on the linked issue so the agent resolves the conflicts and pushes; the normal validate flow then resumes (pr_approved is STICKY — no re-review). Guest PRs get the report only (owner rule 2026-09-21: auto-rework is machine-author-only). Fires once per head: the marker comment carries the head sha and suppresses re-reports for the same head — never the arming (gh-683 bug C, live fa #677/#676 2026-10-03: the marker used to land before arming, a starved dispatch left a reported corpse and the issue was never labelled). Arming lands FIRST, the marker LAST; a marker whose linked issue lacks agent:rework re-arms on the next tick (suppression keys on the label, not the comment).

Auto rework leg: agent:rework armed on the issue either by the review verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED) or by red pre-merge CI. Pushing fixes removes the label (pr_rework removeLabels). prMachineAuthor: auto rework fires ONLY on machine-authored PRs (owner rule) — the machine login is deployment config (jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor / factory-sm machine-author input), never hardcoded; unconfigured fails closed. Manual rework on ANY PR: label the PR agent:rework (see rework-on-label). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run). gh-715 ONE-WINS (live fa gh-1226 2026-10-04 18:47:11/13 — runs 37225765526/37225768365, same head SHA 23dacd10, both dispatched 2s apart by ONE tick): agent:rework can sit on BOTH carriers at once — the issue (this rule) AND the PR (armed by rework-unresolved-threads / the guest validation-red arm) — and each carrier's in-flight guard keys on its own anchor token ('· gh-N' vs '· pr-N'), so both dispatch rules fired for the same work. notPrLabels agent:rework makes this rule defer to the PR-carrier rule whenever the PR is armed: rework-on-label is PR-anchored (the #544-safe anchor), consumes its label on dispatch, and the engine's cross-anchor guard (smAgent triggerWorkflow) suppresses a dispatch while a leg for the SAME issue/PR is already in flight under the other anchor — exactly one leg wins per arm event. No consumeLabels here by design: the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on); the issue-anchored leg itself clears the label via pr_rework removeLabels.

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework (red CI or review CHANGES)

rules.description: Manual rework request: agent:rework label on the PR itself -> rework on demand, ANY author (owner override: a manual label by a write/admin actor fires even on guest PRs). PR-anchored (gh-683 bug E, live fa #1194 2026-10-04: the {issueNumber} body-scrape resolved a stale bare '#327' mention — a wrong-but-EXISTING issue, so the #544 existence guard passed it — while the real linked issue was gh-1044; the factory guard rejected the anchor, run=false, 75s no-op, and the failed consume (bug D) re-fanned it every tick). The label is ON the PR and the rework runs on the PR head, so anchor on inputs.pr directly (the same PR-anchored shape as review-on-label / review-external-once / review-machine-unlinked): preCliReworkSetup's #544 path runs the leg on pr-<N> with no ticket lookup, no scrape, no anchor to mis-resolve. The PR label is consumed on dispatch so the next tick does not re-fire. gh-715: the engine's cross-anchor guard (smAgent triggerWorkflow) also consumes the label when the dispatch is SUPPRESSED because a leg for the same issue/PR is already in flight under the other anchor (e.g. an issue-anchored rework run while this PR-anchored rule matched) — the active run fulfills the request, and consuming prevents a duplicate leg on the next quiet tick; rework-unresolved-threads re-arms the PR if the threads stay unresolved, so the recovery path is intact. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head.

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework label on the PR (manual rework request)

rules.description: Machine-loop completion backfill: an open issue with an open+green MACHINE-authored PR gets ai_developed, which arms review-after-dev. Machine-only (prMachineAuthor) so external PRs never enter the review loop through the backfill; no `in progress` requirement — issues whose dev leg predates the status-label convention (live: fa #503 / PR #676) must still be picked up. Idempotent: ai_developed in notLabels.

GitHub: validated PR (ai_validated latch) after dev -> machine review (never on an armed PR: pr_approved means the review already concluded APPROVED - re-dispatching review duplicates the leg and un-arms the merge queue). OWNER RULE (2026-09-23, validation economy): the latch alone qualifies — no prChecks green requirement. silent-update keeps the head fresh; the review covers the current diff; the FINAL head gets its one pre-merge validation in validate-armed, so a head that moved since the latch's green is safe to review without re-running CI first. Limit 10 (owner 2026-09-22): review legs are plain workflow runs — they parallelize freely; one-per-tick serialized a 12-PR green wave into hours. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: external (non-machine) green PR -> one-time review (PR-anchored; no re-review on later pushes). The machine login is deployment-specific: it arrives via jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (factory-sm input machine-author); with none configured every green PR is reviewable.

inputs.reason: sm: external PR green - one-time review

rules.description: GitHub PR: MACHINE-authored validated PR whose review loop has no leg — the branch/body carry no OPEN linked issue (fix/*, revert/*, chore/* branches), or the linked issue closed: develop-done only backfills OPEN issues, review-after-dev rides the issue carrier, and review-external-once excludes machine authors — so such a PR starves validated-but-never-reviewed forever (live: fa #1068 validated 19h with zero review legs; #1071/#1075 in the same state, owner order 2026-09-30). PR-anchored one-time review, the machine-author twin of review-external-once. NO checks requirement (review-after-dev economy: the ai_validated latch alone qualifies — silent-update keeps the head fresh, the review covers the current diff, and the final pre-merge validation stays in validate-armed post-approve): a green-gated guard would skip silent-updated heads whose rollup reads 'none' (the exact skip that starved the trio). Dedup is structural, not green-gated: the leg runs on the PR head (workflowRef={branch}) so its check run flips the rollup to 'pending' — excluded here — until the runner latches ai_pr_reviewed at the verdict. prMachineAuthor fails CLOSED when no machineAuthor is configured (no auto legs at all). DIRTY heads are NOT excluded: a conflicted unlinked machine PR has no other path to a verdict (conflict-rework's rework re-arm needs the linked issue), and the merge window keeps it out of merges until CLEAN regardless. limit 1: same pacing as review-external-once; the trio drains over consecutive ticks.

inputs.reason: sm: machine PR validated but issue loop never armed a review - one-time review

rules.description: GitHub PR: CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict pinned to an older commit (fixes pushed after the review) + green -> re-arm agent:review. review-on-label dispatches the runner, the runner consumes the label and re-reviews the current head; the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so this never loops. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). agent:rework excluded (#683, 2026-10-04): the ONLY re-review armer that can overlap rework-unresolved-threads (a stale CHANGES_REQUESTED with open threads) — a PR sent to rework must not simultaneously arm a re-review; review-threads-resolved re-arms the review once the threads are resolved. workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: all review threads resolved + the last verdict is older than the head (fixes landed and the threads were worked through) + green -> re-arm agent:review. Covers PR #676: the rework resolves threads (the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict dissolves into COMMENTED), so verdict-staleness alone misses it. Convergent: the re-review's verdict lands on the current head and its fresh threads are unresolved until worked. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).

GitHub PR: validated + reviewed (both latches) + ANY verdict pinned to an older commit + all review threads worked + the head has NO concluded checks (a push moved it after the review — silent-update/rework — so the rollup reads 'none' and every green-gated review path skips) -> RE-REVIEW FIRST (owner 2026-09-29: after ai_validated + a review, a moved head re-runs the REVIEW, never the validation; the single pre-merge validation stays in validate-armed, post-approve, on the final head). Closes the chicken-and-egg stall (live: fa pr-1076 + pr-1075, 2026-09-29 — a machine-authored PR whose head moved after its review stalled until a human label/manual dispatch, tick processed 0). checks 'none' ONLY: 'pending' is the in-flight dispatch bridge — racing it double-dispatches. threadsResolved excludes the mid-rework window (the rework leg owns open threads; its push flips them to resolved and arms THIS rule). Convergent: the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so staleVerdict clears — never loops. Never on approved PRs (pr_approved is sticky — approved rework re-validates, never re-reviews). workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head.

GitHub PR: UNRESOLVED review threads on a machine-authored reviewed PR -> arm agent:rework (dmtools-agents #683, live fa #1194/#1211/#1212 + dart #340, 2026-10-04: all green+reviewed+validated with open threads, heads silently refreshed so the verdicts went stale, and the 04:30 fa tick processed 0 — every re-review armer requires threadsResolved:true, its complement matched NOTHING; extended gh-710, live fa #1211 14:13 re-review: the verdict was APPROVE with 5 new threads — pr_approved + ai_validated + unresolved threads = mergeStateStatus BLOCKED (conversation gate), the old notLabels pr_approved excluded this rule, red-CI rework needs red checks (green), the review-verdict arm fires only on CHANGES_REQUESTED — merge blocked + no armed leg deadlocked the PR ~1h until a manual rework dispatch). Owner rule 2026-10-04: unresolved threads on a machine-authored PR arm agent:rework — the rework leg owns open threads by design (the note in review-stale-verdict-unchecked: threadsResolved 'excludes the mid-rework window (the rework leg owns open threads)'). threadsResolved:false regardless of verdict staleness or value: a FRESH verdict with unresolved threads equally needs rework, and an APPROVE verdict with unresolved threads deadlocks merge without it (staleVerdict or a pr_approved exclusion would only narrow the match back into the blind spot). ORDER/disjointness vs the re-review armers: review-threads-resolved and review-stale-verdict-unchecked require threadsResolved:true — this rule false; one PR can never arm both. agent:review in notLabels keeps a queued/running re-review unstacked, and review-stale-verdict (the one armer without a threads guard) now excludes agent:rework for the same reason. The in-flight guards (the gh-710 gate — unresolved threads > 0 AND no active rework/review/validation): agent:rework (already armed — convergent until the rework leg consumes the label), agent:review (queued/running re-review), ai_validating (merge window), validation_failed (parked). pr_approved is deliberately NOT excluded: the sticky approval is exactly why REWORK is the right leg — after the rework push, validate-armed re-validates the new head and merge proceeds without a re-review (rework re-validates, never re-reviews); review-threads-resolved keeps excluding pr_approved so no review stacks on top. prMachineAuthor fails closed (owner rule: auto-rework is machine-only, same as fail_validation/conflict-rework). localAction arm_rework labels the PR agent:rework + explains in a comment; rework-on-label dispatches the leg (issue-anchored, PR-anchored fallback #544) and consumes the label.

GitHub PR: agent:review label on a PR -> review on demand (any author; consumed by the review runner) workflowRef={branch}: the leg runs on the PR head — GitHub links the run to the PR (visible in PR checks/timeline as the review/rework run).
GitHub: linked PR merged → close the issue (cycle complete)
